topic: front-of-knee pain as a tracking complex, not a single tissue

source.caption:
Knee pain at the front of the knee is rarely one tissue.

When patients walk in describing pain at the kneecap with clicking on flexion, three tissues usually share the load: patellofemoral joint, patellar tendon, medial retinaculum. They live next door to each other. When one starts complaining, the others tend to chime in.

The patella does not glide on rails. Tracking is a balance problem driven by quad pull, IT band tension, hip rotation, and foot mechanics. When the balance shifts, the cap drifts, and the surrounding tissues protest. The clicking the patient feels is real, and it is good information.

I palpate all three structures on the first visit. If two or more are tender and the patient reports clicking, the diagnosis is a tracking complex. The treatment changes immediately. Map all three tender points, test glide and tilt, treat the chain that controls tracking, and reload the knee on purpose.

If your knee clicks, hurts in two or three spots at once, and the standard care keeps stalling, send me a DM and let's map the tracking story.

Be Good. Help Someone. Learn Lots.
